recipes.name: Avocado Soup with Chicken and Lime
ingredients_raw: 8 ounces skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cut into thin strips
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Arrange tortilla strips on a baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until lightly browned, 3 to 5 minutes.

Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook onion, garlic, and jalapenos in oil until lightly browned, 4 to 5 minutes. Stir in chicken, chicken broth, lime juice, tomato, salt and pepper. Gently simmer until chicken is no longer pink, about 10 minutes. Stir in avocado and cilantro and heat through, 3 to 5 minutes. Adjust seasonings to taste.
Ladle soup into bowls and sprinkle with tortilla strips to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Avocado Soup with Chicken and Lime
raw_recipe.description: Strips of chicken breast are simmered in a spicy, citrusy broth, and topped with avocado and crisp corn tortilla strips for a satisfying meal that's ready in about 30 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I am a soup lover. I wanted to make avacado soup and thought I would give this one a try. Wow! I didn't use as many jalapeno's as called for and removed the seeds. Glad I did. Three peppers were just about right for us. This is the perfect soup to accompany your Mexican Food dinner. We had a good Mexican beer with our meal and it was perfect.

The first time I made this, I was not very impressed. No spices- cumin, chili powder, oregano, coriander; and simmering a soup for only 10 minutes does not really allow all the ingredients to get to know each other. I have made this twice since and have changed a lot. I only make it when I have the time. I slow cook the chicken using the "Slow Cooker Carnitas" recipe on this site and use the juices from that to start the soup, adding more stock if needed.

I try to make recipes exactly as written but due to lack of several ingredients I made changes, and it turned out delicious! Substituted a small can of diced tomatoes for whole tomato; used a can of green chilies instead of jalapenos; 1/8 c bottled Key lime juice plus 1 drop lime essential oil in place of limes; 1 drop cilantro essential oil for the cilantro leaves. I sauted the onions and garlic first, then added the frozen chicken breast, broth, tomatoes, and jar of green chilies, salt and pepper, and lime juice. Also added 1 tsp of sugar. To quicken the cook time I used my pressure cooker. To add more color, I also added 2 c shredded purple cabbage, sauted, then added after pressure cooking so they wouldn't get mushy. I added the essential oils when the soup cooled a bit along with the avocado. Remember, a drop of essential oil is all you need!

I have made this recipe several times since finding it, it’s a great base recipe that I have added the following to make it terrific for us. I cook my chicken in the pressure cooker seasoned with salt, pepper, onion powder, garlic powder & Tajin for extra lime flavor. To the broth I add cumin, & chili powder, & riced cauliflower. I brown my onions in bacon fat prior to adding my garlic. I also dump in the drippings from my cooked chicken it adds loads of flavor. Top with fresh cilantro, and sour cream. We substitute Serrano for jalapeños because we prefer it spicy, added some kale for my bowl, I wanted some greens! Great soup for cold weather.

First off...Yum! Thank you for sharing your recipe. I made a few changes to mine due to food preferences. I will make this again. I started with 1 diced carrot in the pan with the onion in 1T of butter and a splash of evoo because that is how I begin my soups. I used about 2-3 diced Anaheim peppers instead of jalapenos, better flavor in my opinion, plus had them on hand. A fellow reviewer mentioned corn, so I added 1/4 c since it seemed a little thin on ingredients, to help with that I also added corn starch/water to thicken it up a bit. I topped it off with a few pieces of avocado. No corn tortillas here, so I just had a warmed up flour one with butter. I added this one to my recipe box.

This soup was phenomenal! I followed the recipe as written except I skipped the jalapeño. After trying a few spoonfuls while it was still cooking, I ended up adding a little extra lime juice (I used the juice of 3 limes total). I ladled over some cooked rice to make it a bit heartier. Refreshing and light!
Fantastic! Like Mexico in a bowl. I recommend doubling the avocado and I puréed half and left half chunky. Also only used one jalapeño because I can't eat spicy food anymore. Will make this again!

Did this in the slow cooker for about 3 hours came out good. I used the whole 4 chiles and 4 fresh limes, but only half an onion and two tomatoes plus doubled the chicken. The first time I made it as the recipe called for it wasn't enough lime or chicken and it was very runny and had way too much onion.

This soup is a refreshing change for chicken soup. I added corn from one ear of corn, a handful of carrot matchsticks, substituted pureed hot peppers for jalapenos, and used harissa oil to sautee. SUPER! I have leftovers frozen for my week-day lunches. Make certain to toast the tortillas enough. I used olive oil Pam and toaster overn.

Love love love this foolproof recipe! Not being a natural at cooking, easy recipes are the best. Cut to the chase and shredded a store-bought roasted chicken and sauteed in garlic and leek, while adding garlic salt and pepper. Added can of corn and diced tomatoes seasoned with basil and oregano. Diced 5 avocados (BIG avocado-loving family) and added teaspoon of cumin. The cumin makes it foolproof, recipe as-written was too bland. The added corn made dish so colorful, my sister immediately posted to Facebook before eating. Thank you for sharing this!

The first time I made this as written and it had waaayyy to much lime. This time I doubled the recipe and only added the juice from half of a small lime. Instead of doubling the tomato, I added a can of Ro-tel. I used rotisserie chicken because I was feeing lazy and let it simmer for 30 minutes to soak up all the flavors. We topped it with the tortilla strips and some queso fresco. Everyone loved it!
Add sour cream to the chicken broth….delicious
I’m with Beth on this. No flavor.
I make it often. It's easy to make, it's quick, and it's delicious.
Very bland. Had to go very rogue to have it flavorful at all.

This is pretty much the recipe for Tortilla Soup that was served in a number of restaurants in Austin, TX, 30 years ago. There are some variants, and it's certainly flexible. I usually crumble in some queso fresco--or feta--at the end and often throw in a handful of frozen corn kernels, too. So often what is called Tortilla Soup is thickened and has too many ingredients. This deliciuos recipe is the real deal!
I love it. I cut the recipe in half because I live by myself. I wish I had made the entire recipe!! I'm 69 years old and don't eat much. But, I'm eating this for lunch and dinner. It's that good!!!
My new favorite soup! Love the cilantro and lime flavor and the chicken and avocado really set it off. Full of flavor and very filling. Has become a new staple in our home.
